# split-plan v2 (replaces Phase B of split-plan.md; Phases A, C and R1–R4 stand)
Phone facts (yours): GPT = 31 entries in a 1-sector array (LBA 2), 4 sectors reserved (LBA 2..5), first usable 6, last usable 31196154, backup header LBA 31196159, disk GUID "WHITECHAPEL LUN1", 4096-B sectors.

## Why not sgdisk --resize-table
Read from gptfdisk source (SetGPTSize): a resize recomputes firstUsableLBA = tableSectors + entriesLBA (=3, not 6), lastUsable = disk - first (31196157, not 31196154) and moves the backup table. That changes header values Google's ABL wrote. split-gpt v2 therefore edits the GPT RAW (python stdlib): only NumberOfPartitionEntries 31→32 (the 32 entries still fit the same single sector and the 4-sector reserved area), the two entry-array CRCs, the two header CRCs, entry 31's start/end and the new entry 32. First/last usable, backup LBA, entries LBA, disk GUID and the other 30 entries stay byte-identical. sgdisk is only used to read and to verify.
Tested: synthetic tables with 31 entries (512-B and exact 4096-B/31196160-sector/first 6/last 31196154/real GUID geometry), checked by real sgdisk 1.0.10 (-p, -v: 'holds up to 32', same usable range, 'No problems found'); negative tests (bad CRC, wrong range, no room, wrong entry) all STOP; restore.sh returns the original bytes.

## Phase B (new)
All commands from the Mac with `ph() { ssh -i "$CHEETAH_SSH_KEY" root@172.16.42.1 "$@"; }`.

**B1 gdisk**: already installed (sgdisk --version = 1.0.10). python3 is required: `ph 'python3 --version'`.

**B2 install split-gpt v2** (sha256 `49b933bad77d27cfd20b59bbe7c1101a9b868ca8fa63e3673b554a31f019d93f`; includes your mknod fix):
`ph 'echo  | base64 -d | gzip -dc > /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt && chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt && sha256sum /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt'`
(Alternative with a file: put split-gpt.sh from the bundle on the Mac and run `ph 'cat > /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt && chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt && sha256sum /usr/local/sbin/split-gpt' < $HOME/cheetah-dual/split/split-gpt.sh`.)

**B3 plan (read-only):** `ph 'split-gpt plan'`
Expect: ...layout rows 31 userdata 14704128 25953023 43941 / 32 ubuntu 2383334 14704101 48128 / tail 20480 MiB, then
`raw GPT edit (dry): sector 4096 B, usable 6..31196154, entries 31 -> 32 (room: 128/128), disk GUID unchanged`
`entry 31 userdata  2383334..31196133  ->  14704128..25953023` / `entry 32 ubuntu new 2383334..14704101 ...` / `(dry run: nothing written)` / `rehearsal OK`.
(room may read 128/128 or 128/32 depending where the backup array sits; both are ≥ 32.) STOP on any "STOP:" line and send it to me.

**B4 backup + copy to Mac + verify** (same as before):
`ph 'split-gpt backup'` then `ph 'tar -C /root -cf - $(cd /root; ls -d gpt-backup-* | tail -1)' > $HOME/cheetah-dual/backup/gpt-backup-A.tar && mkdir -p $HOME/cheetah-dual/backup/gptA && tar -xf $HOME/cheetah-dual/backup/gpt-backup-A.tar -C $HOME/cheetah-dual/backup/gptA && (cd $HOME/cheetah-dual/backup/gptA/gpt-backup-* && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS)` → 3 OK.

**B5 CANARY: raise the entry count only (no partition changes).**
`ph 'systemctl stop systemd-udevd.service systemd-udevd-control.socket systemd-udevd-kernel.socket; split-gpt grow --yes'`
Expect `raw GPT edit (grow): ... entries 31 -> 32`, `written and verified by read-back`, `Partition table holds up to 32 entries`, `First usable sector is 6, last usable sector is 31196154`, `GROWN: 31 -> 32 entries, partitions untouched.`

**B6 let the bootloader read the 32-entry table, THEN decide.**
1. `ph 'sync; reboot'` → Ubuntu must come back (ABL loaded vendor_kernel_boot_b etc. from the new table): `ph 'findmnt -no SOURCE /; sgdisk -p /dev/sda | sed -n "/holds/p;/First usable/p"'` → `/dev/sda31`, `holds up to 32`, `First usable sector is 6, last usable sector is 31196154`.
2. `ph 'reboot-to bootloader'`; Mac: `fastboot getvar current-slot 2>&1 | head -1; fastboot getvar partition-size:userdata 2>&1 | head -1; fastboot getvar partition-size:super 2>&1 | head -1; fastboot getvar all 2>&1 | grep -c has-slot` → `current-slot: b`, a userdata size (still the full 112550 MiB = 118011084800 bytes), a super size, and a non-zero count. Then `fastboot reboot`.
STOP / rollback if: Ubuntu does not return (hold Power+Vol-Down → bootloader; if fastboot answers, flash nothing yet; if the initramfs shell or Ubuntu answers on ssh, run `sh /root/gpt-backup-*/restore.sh` from gpt-backup-A (R2); otherwise see the tail risk below), or fastboot fails to list userdata. Only a clean result here justifies B7.
This canary is what tells us ABL tolerates entries is-not 31, before any layout change is at stake.

**B7 fresh backup of the 32-entry table** (the old backup no longer matches the disk, apply refuses it): repeat B4 with another name (`gpt-backup-B.tar`).

**B8 the split** (same stop-udevd line): `ph 'systemctl stop systemd-udevd.service systemd-udevd-control.socket systemd-udevd-kernel.socket; split-gpt apply --yes'`
Expect: plan, `rehearsal OK`, `raw GPT edit (apply): ... entries 32 -> 32`, `written and verified by read-back`, `No problems found`, last rows `31 ... userdata 14704128 25953023` and `32 ... ubuntu 2383334 14704101`, `GPT written.`
Then `ph 'split-gpt wipe-android'` → `first 4 MiB of Android userdata (sector 14704128) are zero`; `ph 'sync; reboot'`; verify as B6 of split-plan.md (root on /dev/sda32, sda31 userdata ro=1, sda32 ubuntu ro=0).

## Option comparison (honest)
* **32 entries (this plan):** only header count +1; Google's own GPT code in Android (gs101/gs-common bootctrl GptUtils.cpp, read in full) validates only signature, header size 92 and entry size 128 and reads entry_count from the header, with no hard-coded 31 (and it stops at the first nameless entry, so entries must stay contiguous: ours do). Other UFS phones ship 31/32/48/64/128 entries (OnePlus 5: 32, Pixel 2: 48, Lenovo Y700: 32, Xiaomi K30S: 64) and later stock updates change Pixel counts too, so loaders generally key off the header. Unknown: whether Tensor ABL hard-checks 31; no public source. The B5/B6 canary tests exactly that.
* **Reuse an existing entry (no count change):** cheetah LUN0 should be the 31 = 11 unslotted (persist, klog, misc, frp, efs, efs_backup, modem_userdata, metadata, fips, super, userdata) + 10 slotted pairs ×2 (boot, init_boot, vendor_boot, vendor_kernel_boot, dtbo, vbmeta, vbmeta_system, vbmeta_vendor, pvmfw, modem); this matches your 31 exactly [from an XDA bootloader getvar dump; order not verified]. Nothing is unused. Deleting one means: klog/fips (role unknown, ABL may log/verify there), *_b of vbmeta/pvmfw/modem (Android OTA to slot B then fails or ABL refuses slot B), none safe to assume. Worse risk profile than +1 entry.
* **Entry-less raw region (loop/dm on /dev/sda offset):** avoids touching the header, but needs a whole-disk writable node in the initramfs (defeats the guard), invisible to every GPT tool, and a bootloader flash re-uses that space. Only a fallback if the canary shows ABL rejects 32.
* **Abandon the split:** keep slot B + userdata as today (one Android factory reset each time you switch). Costs nothing, zero GPT risk.

## Verdict
Proceed with 32 entries, but ONLY through B5–B6 (canary: count change alone, reboot twice, fastboot check) before B8. Confidence: header/CRC edit is correct and verified on synthetic copies (high); Tensor ABL accepts 32 (medium: no public evidence either way; canary resolves it cheaply). Residual risk: if ABL rejected the table, ABL itself (BL1/BL2/ABL live on other LUNs, untouched) probably still starts and fastboot should respond, restore.sh via dd then needs Linux or a partition:0 flash from the factory image; I cannot verify that fastboot starts with an unreadable GPT — that is the one tail risk (unlikely, since the canary leaves every partition where it is and both copies identical and CRC-valid). Recommendation: do the canary; if anything is odd, abandon.
